claim: For system (1.7) of Cao–Wang–Liu on \(\mathbb R_+^3\), assume \(A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4,B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4,C_1,C_2,C_3,K_1,K_2>0\), \(k_1,k_2\ge0\), \(0\le m_1,m_2\le1\), and \(q_iE_i\ge0\). Set \(R_1=A_1-q_1E_1\), \(R_2=B_1-q_2E_2\), \(M_1=K_1\max\{R_1,0\}/A_2\), \(M_2=K_2\max\{R_2,0\}/B_2\), \(D=C_3+q_3E_3\), and \(\Gamma=C_1(1-m_1)M_1+C_2(1-m_2)M_2-D\). If \(\Gamma<0\), then every compact invariant set is contained in the predator-free plane \(y=0\). Consequently every compactly supported invariant probability measure is supported on the equilibrium set of the predator-free planar competitive subsystem; in particular, no periodic, quasiperiodic, or chaotic compact recurrent dynamics can have positive predator density under this threshold.

correctness.rationale: For any compact invariant set, two-sided maxima of the prey coordinates force \(x_1\le M_1\) and \(x_2\le M_2\). Under \(\Gamma<0\), the exact identity for \(d(\log y)/dt\) is uniformly negative; any complete orbit with \(y>0\) would therefore grow without bound backward in time, contradicting compactness. On \(y=0\), the exact Dulac divergence is strictly negative in the open quadrant; one-dimensional boundary flows have no non-equilibrium recurrence. Poincare recurrence then puts every compact invariant probability measure on equilibria. Assumptions and quantifiers are explicit, and no finite experiment is promoted to an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly studies Hopf bifurcation and chaotic behavior, so a parameter-explicit region in which all positive-predator compact recurrence is impossible answers a natural global dynamical question. It upgrades a local predator-invasion condition at one equilibrium to a uniform statement over every compact invariant set and supplies a stationary-measure classification. The result is structurally motivated by refuge and harvesting rather than by an arbitrary parameter slice.
